facts.class_title_and_tools: Class 1: Runway to the AI World and the LLM Landscape. Tools: Google Colab, a web browser, a terminal.
facts.setting_expectations: The class is intentionally light and introductory: no heavy coding, no difficult theory, no overwhelming jargon. Frame it as entering a new city for the first time: learn what exists, what things are called and how they connect, not build skyscrapers. The goal is that AI feels less mysterious by the end.
facts.by_the_end_learners_can: Use the terms AI, LLM, GenAI, AI Agent and Agentic AI correctly; navigate Google Colab (run cells, edit code, restart runtimes); explain what an API is and why AI tools depend on it; read a basic JSON response; feel comfortable when terminal commands or GitHub appear later; explain how frontend, backend, database and APIs fit together in an AI application.
facts.what_this_class_is_not: A runway, not the flight. Not covered today: prompt engineering, API keys, system prompts, AI agents in depth, production deployments, advanced workflows. Each gets a dedicated session later.
facts.teaching_style: Very conversational: stories, analogies, demos, intuition and practical examples. The goal is to feel at home in the AI world, not to memorise definitions.
facts.section_pattern: For each term or tool: a plain-English definition, one everyday example, one picture or diagram, then a one-question checkpoint quiz with the answer and a spoken explanation of why the other options fail.
facts.analogies_used: AI as an umbrella: transportation, then motor vehicles, then electric vehicles, then a Tesla for an LLM. An LLM as autocomplete. An API as a vending machine. A context window as the model's desk. Temperature as a creativity dial. Choosing an LLM like choosing a programming language. The LLM landscape like the cloud providers AWS, GCP and Azure.
facts.tooling_cells: Short runnable Colab cells marked TRY IT NOW (Shift + Enter), for example a cell that prints a confirmation, then one the learner edits and runs.
facts.first_prompt_demo: Give the same prompt to three chat tools (free tiers), and ask learners to compare length, structure, confidence, depth, personality and extras. There is no right answer; the point is to build a sense of each model's personality.
facts.accounts_checklist: Learners set up the AI accounts the course needs (some need email verification and a payment method). The exact list is [[FROM_SME: accounts learners must set up before class]]. If they hit issues they flag them and the instructor troubleshoots together.
facts.interaction_note: The source script opens with a show of hands. Online, use a chat poll instead (rule E3).
facts.closing: A decision framework for choosing a model, a one-table summary of every term and tool covered, and a list of key links.
